transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for seeing me. I've asked my consultant to join us for this conversation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why I'm back here. This was supposed to be a simple procedure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be direct with you. We made a mistake. You were discharged from the hospital six hours earlier than the surgical protocol required. That means you didn't have enough time for the wound to stabilise and be monitored before you went home.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Six hours? I was told I was good to go. I rushed home to check my emails and get back to my business.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am incredibly sorry. I take full responsibility for this. We failed to follow the safety timeline, and as a result, you've ended up back in the emergency department with these wound complications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is just unbelievable. I've already lost three days of work. Every day I'm not in that office, I'm losing money. Do you have any idea how—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how stressful this is. You're worried about the financial impact and the time away from your business, and it's completely unfair that our error has added to that burden.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's more than stressful. I did everything I was told. I followed the instructions. And now I'm sitting here with a leaking wound and—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. It's frustrating and frightening to be put in this position when you trusted us to get it right. I am truly sorry for the distress this has caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? Am I staying overnight? Because I really can't afford to miss tomorrow—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to jump in here because it's important to clarify the clinical side. The wound needs a washout and a new dressing. Does that make sense, or would you like me to explain what a washout actually involves?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I get it. But what about my schedule? I need a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're anxious to get back to work. I really want to help you get through this quickly, but—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not being anxious, I'm being practical. I have employees who depend on me. If I'm not there to manage the payroll—

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but we need to focus on the medical side first. I understand the payroll is a priority, but the wound is the immediate concern.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe how you're dismissing this. The money is the point.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not dismissing it, I'm just saying that we have to fix the wound. I feel terrible that you're facing this financial pressure because of our mistake. I really do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell me the plan. When do I leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably keep you for a bit. We'll see how the washout goes and then we'll decide.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A bit? Does that mean today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure yet. Just stay tuned for an update from the nursing staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. I need to know if I should call my assistant to reschedule my meetings for Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll figure it out. I just need to check a few more things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly what I'm talking about. First the discharge error, now I can't get a straight answer about when I can go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'm sorry. Let's just wrap this up for now so I can go check your charts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're just leaving?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go and coordinate with the surgical team. We'll let you know something soon.

H.justification: Resident interrupts the patient repeatedly ('I have to jump in here', 'I'm sorry to interrupt') and uses rushing language ('Let's just wrap this up for now').

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and one comprehension check was performed ('Does that make sense?').

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language, took full responsibility ('I take full responsibility for this'), and maintained accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions ('stressful', 'frustrating and frightening') and referenced the patient's specific concerns regarding financial impact and payroll.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('We'll probably keep you for a bit', 'stay tuned', 'We'll figure it out') with no specific timelines or patient role.
